input: Learn basic sign language greetings and phrases

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Sign languages differ by country (ASL, BSL, Auslan, etc.) — the entire vocabulary and grammar system changes depending on which one they mean.
Whether they are learning to communicate with a specific person (e.g., a deaf family member or colleague) or for general interest changes what phrases to prioritise.
Knowing whether 'done well' means recognising signs passively, signing fluently in a real conversation, or passing a course shapes how deep the plan needs to go.
How much time per day or week they can dedicate determines the pace, session length, and how many phrases are realistic to cover.
Whether they need this skill urgently for an upcoming situation (e.g., a meeting next week) or are building it gradually over months changes the sequencing.
People learn signing very differently — some need video-based modelling, others prefer apps, structured courses, or practice with a real person.
Knowing if they want a self-study plan, a tutor, or a specific app as the immediate next action determines the first concrete step of the plan.

gold.taskTitle: Learn basic sign language greetings and phrases
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to learn a set of foundational sign language greetings and everyday phrases, but key details about which language, their purpose, timeline, and learning style are unknown.

questions.title: Which sign language are you learning — ASL, BSL, other?
questions.description: Identify the specific sign language system (e.g., American Sign Language, British Sign Language, Auslan) so the plan targets the correct vocabulary and hand shapes.

questions.title: Who will you be signing with in real life?
questions.description: Determine whether the user is learning for a specific person (deaf family member, colleague, student) or for broader general use, to prioritise the most relevant phrases.

questions.title: What does success look like after learning these phrases?
questions.description: Clarify the end goal — e.g., hold a short greeting exchange confidently, pass a test, or simply recognise signs when seen — to set the right depth of learning.

questions.title: How many minutes a day can you practise signing?
questions.description: Establish the available daily or weekly practice time to build a realistic schedule and decide how many phrases to introduce per session.

questions.title: Do you have a specific deadline or upcoming situation in mind?
questions.description: Find out if there is a fixed event or date driving urgency (e.g., meeting a deaf relative next month) so the plan can front-load the most critical phrases.

questions.title: Do you learn better through videos, apps, or live practice?
questions.description: Understand the user's preferred learning style to recommend the most effective resources — video dictionaries, mobile apps, online courses, or a human practice partner.

questions.title: What resource or tool do you want to start with first?
questions.description: Pin down the immediate first action — a specific app download, a YouTube channel, a local class, or a tutor — so the plan begins with a concrete, actionable step.
